BLOCKED: PR #71 implements this issue's full Task section, but the required `code-review` check has not gone green after 10 review-and-fix rounds, and I don't believe further rounds will resolve it — this needs a human decision, not more iteration.

## What's done

PR #71 (`feat/issue-26` → `develop`) implements the sync core in full: three adapters (IMAP/imapflow, Gmail REST, Graph REST) over one shared schema, JWZ threading, deterministic People-linking, reversible credential encryption, memory-safe streaming attachment processing (including a size cap on all three adapters), HTML sanitization, Postgres full-text search (with recency-blended ranking and a thin layer of Gmail-style search operators), PDF/DOCX attachment text extraction, a periodic search-reindex safety net, and the Gmail-in-IMAP-fallback-mode label handling. `ci` and `review` (the other two required checks) both pass. The build is clean and all 161 backend tests pass.

Across the 10 review rounds, every *concrete, file-and-line* finding the bot raised was investigated and either fixed or (for two specific findings, with inline reasoning posted on the PR) shown to be a false positive against the actual code (`createItemRelation`'s own `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE`, and `personLinkingActions.ts` being a deterministic trigger action, not agent-originated). The last three consecutive rounds report **zero open findings** from that mechanism — a real, converged, positive signal.

## Why I'm stopping here

The `code-review` check's *other* mechanism — a per-run "acceptance criteria" table checked against the full spec text — has not converged and I don't believe it will:

- The total criterion count and pass count fluctuate substantially between runs (50/69, 63/80, 65/82, 55/78, 50/66 across the last five rounds alone) with no apparent memory of previous rounds' resolutions, unlike the findings mechanism.
- Several items are re-flagged as blocking in every single round regardless of code changes, including ones I can point at concrete evidence against — e.g. round 10 again flags "no `item_id REFERENCES items(id)`" as blocking, which is the same deliberate, documented, repo-wide precedent from issues #21/#24/#25 (`items` is `PARTITION BY LIST (database_id)`; Postgres doesn't allow a plain FK into a partitioned table) — not something new to this PR, and not something this PR could "fix" without revisiting schema decisions made three issues ago. I added a regression test this round specifically disproving another repeatedly-recycled claim ("UIDVALIDITY reset leaves stale/duplicate folder edges") — the test passes, confirming the code was already correct, and the criterion was still re-flagged as unmet in the immediately following round.
- The remaining recurring items (IMAP IDLE, bidirectional flag write-back, CONDSTORE flag-only sync, watch/subscription-derived timing, Gmail Pub/Sub push, Graph webhooks) all trace back to one structural gap: this issue's own Task section doesn't add a `read`/`flags` property to the Emails schema, and no "mark as read" UI action exists yet to originate a write in either direction — that's issue #27's surface, not #26's. IDLE/push/webhooks need a long-lived composition-root process that no adapter in this PR (or issue #25's equivalent) stands up yet, matching the established "inject the real implementation later" pattern this whole module follows.
- A couple of items are literal-library-naming pedantry (the issue text says `pdftotext`; I used `pdf-parse`, a pure-JS equivalent, specifically to avoid requiring an OS-level binary in every deployment — the same reasoning already accepted for the pre-existing hunspell deviation, which itself still gets re-flagged every round despite being justified since the very first commit on this PR).

Full point-by-point reasoning for each recurring item is on the PR (three review-reply comments, https://github.com/dvdtrsnk/semprec/pull/71#issuecomment-5455953527 onward).

## What a human needs to decide

1. Whether the `code-review` gate's acceptance-criteria mechanism should be relaxed/reconfigured for issues like this one, where the linked issue is one part of a larger spec section and intentionally defers real chunks of functionality to sibling issues (#27, #31, #40) or to established repo-wide precedent — or whether it's expected to eventually converge and I should have kept iterating.
2. Whether the still-genuinely-missing pieces (IMAP IDLE / bidirectional flag sync / push-notification setup — all blocked on the same schema/UI gap; concurrent-insert hardening beyond what `message_id`'s `ON CONFLICT` already provides) should be split into an explicit follow-up issue, or folded into #27 where the schema surface they need will actually get added.
3. Whether to manually override the required check for this PR, or ask me to keep going — my read is further rounds will keep re-litigating the same items without new information, but I could be wrong about that.

The branch is pushed and up to date; PR #71 is open and mergeable except for the blocked check. I have not merged it or closed this issue.

Merged to develop as eec0c081e65a02c09a263ee0c64003cb006df4b7 (human-assisted, not the automated pipeline).

The findings mechanism of the `code-review` check converged cleanly (three consecutive rounds, zero open findings). The check's separate acceptance-criteria mechanism kept fluctuating (50/69 → 63/80 → 65/82 → 55/78 → 50/66 across rounds) and repeatedly re-flagged items that were independently verified as either: deliberate precedent from #21 (`items` is `PARTITION BY LIST (database_id)`, so a plain FK isn't possible), out of this issue's scope and owned by #27 (mailbox UI — read/flags), or a justified library substitution (`pdf-parse` instead of `pdftotext`, avoiding an OS-level binary dependency).

Given that verification, `code-review` was temporarily removed from develop's required status checks, this PR was merged, and the requirement was restored immediately after (confirmed: `enforce_admins` was never touched, back to ["review","code-review","ci"]).

The genuinely-deferred sync infrastructure (IMAP IDLE, bidirectional flag write-back, Gmail Pub/Sub push, Graph webhooks) is tracked in a new follow-up issue.
